description: Repair ready_tasks(tasks, capacity) to validate task dependencies and select dispatchable work subject to global capacity and exclusive resources.
requirements: Tasks are dicts with unique string id, optional depends_on list of task IDs, optional resources list of string resource IDs, optional integer priority (default 0), and status pending/running/done/failed (default pending). Inputs otherwise follow this schema.

Validate capacity is an integer >=0, rejecting bool and other types with ValueError. Reject duplicate task IDs, unknown dependencies and any dependency cycle with ValueError, even if all tasks in a cycle are done or capacity is zero.
Capacity is the maximum total number of running tasks, so each existing running task consumes one slot. Never return more than max(0, capacity - running_count) new task IDs.
Only pending tasks whose every dependency has status done can be selected. Failed or running prerequisites do not count as done; unrelated branches remain eligible.
Resources held by existing running tasks cannot be selected again. Newly selected tasks immediately reserve their resources, so selected tasks also cannot conflict with one another.

Consider eligible tasks by descending priority, retaining original input order on ties. Greedily skip conflicting tasks and continue to later candidates until slots are filled or candidates end; do not globally optimize scheduling.
Return selected IDs in dispatch order and preserve inputs unchanged. Done/failed tasks hold no resources.

provenance.description: This is an original coordination stress fixture grounded in the repository's documented dependency and single-owner concerns. No production scheduler or historical defect was copied; it is not representative benchmark data.

validity_limits: Calibration only; these tasks do not establish representative development performance or generality.
Hidden tests are independent of the solving run, not independently authored from this fixture's reference implementation.
The oracle is one valid implementation, not an exact patch requirement; behavioral alternatives are allowed.
Passing visible tests is intentionally insufficient. Base failure is seeded and does not predict model failure rate.
